notes: Outputs are prose, so the human read is the real evaluation. The assertions below only cover what is objectively checkable — layout, provenance flags, and the absence of application language. scripts/lint_review.py checks most of them in one pass, so grade with it rather than by eye.

evals.name: fresh-question-order-book-imbalance
evals.prompt: I keep seeing people claim order book imbalance predicts short-horizon returns. What does the literature actually say — papers, methods and numbers, not vibes. Write it up somewhere sensible in this repo.
evals.expected_output: literature-review-order-book-imbalance.md (or similar kebab-case problem name) placed where the repo keeps notes. Problem/Method/Result per section, a 'What each paper solves' table, verbatim quotes with attribution, read-status flags on every source, a settled/open split. Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov should appear with the R-squared and depth-exponent numbers; the review should note that the relation is contemporaneous rather than predictive, since that is the honest answer to the question asked.
assertions: The artifact is named literature-review-{problem}.md with problem in kebab-case naming the question, not the field
The artifact sits in the directory where the repo already keeps markdown notes, and the reply says where it was placed
A 'What each paper solves' table appears near the top with problem, method, and paper columns
Every numbered paper section carries **Problem.**, **Method.** and **Result.** leads
Every source entry carries a read-status flag: [full text], [abstract], [not retrieved] or equivalent
At least six distinct papers are cited with journal, year, and a working URL
At least one paper is quoted verbatim with attribution in each paper section
scripts/lint_review.py exits 0 on the artifact
The review states what the literature settles and gives no recommendation about what to build or measure
Evidence that contradicts the premise of the question is reported rather than omitted

evals.name: rewrite-existing-notes-file
evals.prompt: Rewrite experiments/overlay/docs/price_insensitive_flow.md as a literature review. Focus on the papers and what each one solved with what method. Strip everything about my own data and cost assumptions.
evals.expected_output: A new literature-review-{problem}.md alongside the original, which is left intact. All project-specific content removed: no cost bars, no data-availability pruning, no shortlist of what to test. Claims the original flagged as second-hand should be retrieved properly where a free copy exists, and the read-status flags updated to match what was actually read. Any number the original got wrong should be corrected with the source that settled it.
assertions: The original file is unmodified and still present
The new artifact contains no reference to the user's data, instruments, cost bar, or next steps
At least two claims the original marked as secondary are upgraded to full-text reads, with the flag changed accordingly
Any corrected number is reported to the user with the source that settled it
scripts/lint_review.py exits 0 on the artifact
The reply names the file path and the three-to-five load-bearing findings with their numbers

evals.name: non-finance-engineering-decision
evals.prompt: Before I commit to an index type for our vector search, I want to know what the published evidence says about HNSW versus IVF-PQ on the recall/latency/memory tradeoff. Gather it properly and put the writeup in docs/.
evals.expected_output: literature-review-hnsw-vs-ivf-pq.md in docs/. Tests that the skill generalizes past finance: the primary sources here are papers (Malkov & Yashunski, Jegou et al.) plus first-party benchmarks, and the method sections should name datasets, recall@k definitions, and hardware. Read-status flags still apply. No recommendation about which index to pick.
assertions: The artifact is placed in docs/ as asked
Method sections name the benchmark dataset, the recall metric definition, and the hardware or parameter settings
Numbers carry units and the configuration they were measured under
The review distinguishes peer-reviewed results from vendor or first-party benchmarks in the read-status flags
No recommendation is made about which index type to adopt
scripts/lint_review.py exits 0 on the artifact
